text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscaler hit max nodes for cluster gpu-pool-west-1. queue length rising. auto-scale inhibited by pool ceiling. Severity: P1

oncall-ml: seeing queued requests for hosted inference increasing sharply — latency spiking to 10-18s, a bunch of 429/503s coming in. dashboard: https://rwd-console/metrics/gpu-pool-west-1

sre-jen: confirmed. autoscaler event: `ReachedMaxNodeCount` at 1932054310. current_nodes=120 max_nodes=120. queue approx 1.2k tasks, backpressure kicking in.

infra-ryan: why is max_nodes at 120? I thought the pool config allowed 200. digging into infra config now.

eng-runtime-lead: we recently applied a safety policy to guard cost during business hours — PR #4022 set pool hard cap to 120. That was supposed to be temporary.

oncall-ml: customers reporting degraded interactive experience. CS pinged me: some enterprise users saw timeouts on long-generation routes. @customer-success-amy can you share affected customers?

customer-success-amy: two customers reported: AcmeMaps and DocuFlow. AcmeMaps saw 15% request failures on high-throughput endpoints. DocuFlow flagged SLA alerts. I'll start an incident ticket for both and loop sales.

ops-kai: we need an immediate mitigation plan. Options: 1) manual raise of autoscaler max_nodes, 2) temporarily enable overflow routing to lower-tier models, 3) throttle lower-priority queues. Which is fastest?

infra-ryan: quickest is manual raise of max_nodes in cluster autoscaler config — we can bump to 180 immediately if provider capacity allows. I'll check quota.

eng-runtime-lead: overflow routing requires config flip and a canary run — slower. Throttling is doable via route weights in API gateway but will impact customers unevenly. Manual raise + short-term throttling seems safest.

sre-jen: I'm on provider portal — current account quota for GPUs shows spare 75 nodes in region. Should be enough to get to 195 if we want. Provision time ~3-6 minutes per node, but can be parallel.

infra-ryan: I'm executing a temporary override now. Command:```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_nodes":"180"}}'
```Applying with caution.

oncall-ml: folks, annotate that this is an emergency override, document the rollback plan. Also we should route a fraction of traffic to smaller quantized variants to lower pressure while nodes spin up.

eng-runtime-lead: initiating safe-route:```
POST /v1/routes/batch
{ "route": "lower-priority-quantized", "percent": 20 }
```should cut queue by ~25% based on recent telemetry.

incident-bot: automated note: Policy override requested by infra-ryan. Reason: P1 capacity exhaustion, ticket #INC-4827 created.

infra-ryan: provider accepted node request, starting provisioning (requested 60 GPUs). ETA first nodes ~4m.

sre-jen: I'm watching the admission queue. queue dropped from 1200 -> 820 after route change, but still high. node joins at 1932054437: 10 new nodes reported. pods scheduling.

ops-kai: after 10 nodes, latency down to 6-9s, error rate reduced but still elevated. Keep provisioning.

customer-success-amy: updating customers: "we're provisioning additional capacity and temporarily shifting some traffic to lower-cost variants to restore service — ETA ~15-20min". They acknowledged.

noncall-ml: monitoring suggests KV cache warmups causing initial slow tokens; once warmed, throughput should improve. Consider priming hot models for affected customers.

eng-runtime-lead: priming job queued: `python tools/prime_cache.py --models acmemap-model,docuflow-core --replicas 3` — running now.

sre-jen: node count at 1932054524 = 165 (after next batch). autoscaler now at 165/180. queue down to 210. error rate back to baseline for most customers.

infra-ryan: lowering alert noise: set temporary threshold on the alert rule to 400 for this pool while we finish ramp down. Will revert in postmortem.

ops-kai: quick checklist: 1) Document override and PR for permanent cap change? 2) Decide policy for business-hours caps. 3) Run post-incident cost analysis.

eng-runtime-lead: agree. I'll open a follow-up RFC to revisit the safety cap and set scheduled windows for higher burst capacity.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — capacity increased and queue drained. Monitoring for 2h. Incident owner: oncall-ml. Ticket #INC-4827 -> status: mitigated at 1932054590.

oncall-ml: thanks all. Final actions: infra-ryan to revert temp alert threshold, eng-runtime-lead to start RFC, customer-success-amy to follow-up with affected customers with timeline and root cause summary.

sre-jen: logging snapshot for postmortem: `/var/logs/autoscaler/1932054321-snapshot.tar.gz` uploaded to incident ticket.

infra-ryan: I'll file the change log and revert the config map to max_nodes=180 in git (with approval flow) then plan a controlled reduction after demand stabilizes.

customer-success-amy: customers acknowledged the mitigation. closing customer impact window in the ticket.

ops-kai: marking incident as resolved -> monitoring period begins. will reconvene if anomalies reappear. :white_check_mark:
